{{Short description|Topological space}}
{{About-distinguish-text|Arens–Fort space|[https://topology.pi-base.org/spaces/S156 Arens space]}}

[[File:ArensFortSpace ZeroNeighbourhood.svg|thumb|238x238px|Example neighborhood of (0,0) in the Arens–Fort space]]
In [[mathematics]], the '''Arens–Fort space''' is a special example in the theory of [[topological space]]s, named for [[Richard Friederich Arens]] and [[M. K. Fort, Jr.]]

== Definition ==
The Arens–Fort space is the topological space <math>(X,\tau)</math> where <math>X</math> is the set of ordered pairs of non-negative [[integer]]s <math>(m, n).</math> A subset <math>U \subseteq X</math> is [[open set|open]], that is, belongs to <math>\tau,</math> if and only if:
* <math>U</math> does not contain <math>(0, 0),</math> or
* <math>U</math> contains <math>(0, 0)</math> and also all but a finite number of points of all but a finite number of columns, where a column is a set <math>\{ (m, n) ~:~ 0 \leq n \in \mathbb{Z} \}</math> with <math>0 \leq m \in \mathbb{Z}</math> fixed. 

In other words, an open set is only "allowed" to contain <math>(0, 0)</math> if only a finite number of its columns contain significant gaps, where a gap in a column is significant if it omits an infinite number of points.

== Properties ==

It is 
* [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]]
* [[regular space|regular]]
* [[normal space|normal]]

It is not:
* [[second-countable]]
* [[first-countable]]
* [[metrizable]]
* [[compact space|compact]]
* [[Sequential space|sequential]]
* [[Fréchet–Urysohn space|Fréchet–Urysohn]]

There is no sequence in <math>X \setminus \{ (0, 0) \}</math> that converges to <math>(0, 0).</math> However, there is a sequence <math>x_{\bull} = \left( x_i \right)_{i=1}^{\infty}</math> in <math>X \setminus \{ (0, 0) \}</math> such that <math>(0, 0)</math> is a [[cluster point]] of <math>x_{\bull}.</math>{{cn|date=December 2025}}
